concept.title: Wi-Fi Access Point
concept.shortdesc: A Wi Fi access point provides wireless connectivity to devices on a network. It enables devices to connect to the network without using Ethernet cables.

section.title: Overview
section.p: A Wi Fi access point (AP) is a networking device that broadcasts a wireless signal for client devices.
In this guide, the provides wireless access to the network for Wi Fi-enabled devices.

section.title: Role of a Wi Fi Access Point
section.p: A Wi Fi access point enables wireless devices to communicate with the local network and access Internet services.
It receives data from wireless devices and forwards the data to the network through a wired connection.
The access point also receives network traffic and transmits it to connected wireless devices.

section.title: How a Wi Fi Access Point Works
section.p: The connects to the through an Ethernet connection.
It broadcasts a wireless network that devices can detect and connect to.
Wireless devices connect to the network by selecting the SSID .

section.title: When to Use a Wi Fi Access Point
section.p: A dedicated Wi Fi access point can improve wireless coverage in areas where the router signal is weak.
Additional access points are commonly used in large homes or buildings that require extended wireless coverage.
